purpose: Reconstruct the frozen heldout Layer-B geometry from the response-independent 71-node coordinate registry and frozen world family, conditioned only on source identities already recorded in the consumed result artifact. No biological response is reopened and no model is refit.

established: Once source identity and the fully surviving five-world family are fixed, the heldout Layer-B matrix is generated entirely from frozen geography/topology.
For both source identities observed across the five folds, all 71 stable nodes have distinct Layer-B vectors.
The surviving-world fraction and positive-support fraction are constant across all nodes; the remaining variation is a six-dimensional centered geometry signature.
The response-independent reconstruction reproduces the consumed artifact feature fingerprints exactly.
structural_interpretation.mechanism_implication: The Tampa heldout Layer-B block is an injective node-level spatial signature under each observed source anchor, rather than a representation carrying fold-specific world-set contraction. Reusing that signature across repeated visits makes node identity/spatial geometry available to the augmented learner in an additional nonlinear encoding.
structural_interpretation.not_established: This audit alone does not prove that the unique node signature caused the observed log-loss degradation; it identifies a concrete representation property to test prospectively.
